summary: Feed s179_triple to IDS is degraded: 3 high-severity faults - 83.2% encrypted traffic exceeds 60% tolerance, VLAN 20 missing with 49% untagged, and 9.2% TCP packet drops causing incomplete flows for IDS inspection.

findings.root_cause: 83.2% of bytes are encrypted vs IDS tolerance of 60%. Traffic is predominantly TLS/encrypted without broker-side decryption or plaintext forwarding, so IDS sees only handshakes.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload for signature and anomaly detection; with 83% encrypted it is blind to payloads, drastically reducing detection coverage and allowing threats to hide in encrypted channels.

recommended_fix.why: IDS cannot inspect encrypted payloads; decrypt at broker/decryption zone or feed decrypted copy to restore visibility within tool's 60% tolerance.

findings.root_cause: Required VLAN 20 not seen and 49% of packets are untagged. VLAN tags are being stripped between TAP/SPAN and IDS - likely packet broker configured to strip tags or SPAN trunk not forwarding VLAN 20.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS expects VLANs 10 and 20 for segmentation/policy. Missing VLAN 20 means half the intended traffic is invisible or misclassified, creating coverage gaps and incorrect tenant/policy attribution.

recommended_fix.why: Restore 802.1Q tags for VLAN 20 at broker egress so IDS receives correctly tagged traffic for both required VLANs.

findings.root_cause: 233 of 2523 TCP packets (9.2%) show gaps/retransmissions exceeding 1% threshold. Indicates drops in SPAN/broker fabric before IDS - oversubscription, buffer exhaustion, or 1G tool port congestion - not tool overload itself (tool_overload healthy).
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs both directions and full payload for stream reassembly. 9% loss causes broken flows, missed signatures, failed file extraction, and attacker evasion via gaps.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute load and eliminate drops by load-balancing across IDS pool or upgrading feed capacity; also verify SPAN vs TAP and broker buffers to stop 9% loss.
